g.text: IN PLAIN ENGLISH
Work backward from playback, reserving time for later steps.
Then subtract the earliest allowed start to find the available budget.
The same bar has different deadlines for speech, preparation and playback.
P: playback timestamp; M: reserve after this stage; D: latest finish.
R: earliest allowed start; b: available duration. All values here use milliseconds.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #2f6bdb

g.text: WORKED RAP EXAMPLE
A bar must start playing at P = 8,000 ms.
For prepared audio, reserve M = 200 ms.
That total already includes the early-freeze guard.
Required work can begin at R = 4,000 ms.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #2f6bdb

g.text: Available budget: 3,800 ms
The 200-ms margin is illustrative, not a tuned default.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #2f6bdb

g.text: WHAT THIS TELLS US
Lookahead becomes useful only after the required inputs are ready. Reserve each later step once.
If the stage becomes ready after its deadline, its available budget is already negative.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #2f6bdb
